notes: Found with WebSearch, then read with WebFetch (page text summarised by a small model, so figures are as that summary reported them). Every entry's source_url is a page that was fetched and that itself names the investor; facts seen only in search snippets are in gaps. Investor names are as each source gives them (Bynd Venture Capital was formerly Busy Angels; Bright Pixel was formerly Sonae IM). No websummit.com, lu.ma, luma.com, meetup.com or eventbrite pages were fetched. Reviewed by startups.b@PrompTugal.dinis on 19 November 2026: each source page re-read in its raw HTML; every amount and every investor name matched.

entries.name: Meight seed round
investors: European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT)
entries.what: Portuguese freight-transport software startup Meight closed a seed round led by Faber to expand its AI platform for road freight operations and to recruit.
entries.how_read: WebFetch summary of the ECO article; the date is the article's publication date and the article does not state the company's base city

entries.name: Meight seed round (second)

entries.name: Chic by Choice financing round
entries.what: Portuguese designer-dress rental startup Chic by Choice closed a financing round led by its existing shareholders, including Faber Ventures. This is older than 2022 and is kept only because it names Faber Ventures.
entries.how_read: WebFetch summary of the Dinheiro Vivo article; the date is the article's publication date, the round type is not stated, and the company's base city is not stated

entries.name: Delox Series A
entries.what: Delox, a University of Lisbon spin-off that makes a bio-decontamination device for laboratory equipment, closed a Series A led by Beta Capital for certification, production and entry to European and North American markets.
entries.how_read: WebFetch summary of the Business-IT article; the date is the article's publication date; Lisbon is inferred from the team working at Tec Labs of the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Lisbon, the article does not name the city Place set to national by startups.b@ on review: the source does not name the company's city (it was inferred as lisboa).

entries.name: Azitek investment round
entries.what: Azitek, which develops IoT asset-tracking technology for industry, raised a round led by Beta Capital to enter other European markets.
entries.how_read: WebFetch summary of the Business-IT article; the date is the article's publication date and the round type is not stated; Porto is inferred from the company being incubated at UPTEC, the article does not name its base city Place set to national by startups.b@ on review: the source does not name the company's city (it was inferred as porto).

gaps.why: Search results only showed the Fund III close and Lisbon office (October 2026); Granter's round (tech.eu, 2026-11-03) and the Augusta Labs article (24noticias, 2026-06-16) were read and do not name BY Venture Partners. Search snippets linking BY to Granter and Augusta Labs were not confirmed, so nothing is recorded.

gaps.why: Only search snippets seen: WeatherPromise (a US insurtech, January 2026) and directory listings (Fraudio is Amsterdam-based). The Granter article does not name Big Start Ventures. Not fetched, so not recorded.

gaps.what: Hovione Capital (now Bionova Capital): no Portuguese round found naming Hovione Capital
gaps.why: The 2019 CellmAbs article names only Portugal Ventures. The firm rebranded in February 2021 and its Vaxdyn deal is Spanish.

gaps.what: Sonae IM (now Bright Pixel): no round in a Portuguese-based startup found
gaps.why: Sellforte (Finnish, EUR 4 million, 2021-03-23) was read and names Sonae IM, but it is not a Portuguese company, so it is left out. Recent Bright Pixel deals seen in search are in foreign companies. Jscrambler (Porto, 2018, led by Sonae IM) was seen only in snippets because the page refused.

gaps.what: Busy Angels: no round naming the old name found
gaps.why: The firm has traded as Bynd Venture Capital since 2019. Reveni (Madrid) names Bynd but is Spanish, so it is left out. Fund III first investments Equall, CircuitLeap and Spot were seen in snippets without amounts or dates.
